slots.writingObjective: State as a fact about TextOS that the questions it measures are the exact list a person approved.
One sentence for a search result: TextOS proposes the questions, a person approves the list, and the version measured is exactly the one approved.

Open on the reader's situation: a tool that tells you how often AI assistants mention you is only as honest as the list of questions it asks, and that list is usually chosen for you, out of sight. Say that this note explains how the list is proposed, grounded and approved.
slots.buyerIntent: Who decides which questions I am measured on?

slots.heading: How can I approve the list of questions I want to be measured on?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: TextOS drafts candidate questions from traced sources and labels where each one comes from; demand comes from imported, dated sources and is not a measure of real traffic; a person approves the list, and approving and launching the measurement are a single gate; the measured panel is exactly the approved version.
slots.buyerIntent: How can I approve the list of questions I want to be measured on?

slots.heading: Each question says where it came from
slots.writingObjective: Explain that a question drafted inside TextOS from traced sources keeps that origin until it is approved; that later demand data does not relabel how it was formulated; and that how a question is worded, whether demand for it is proven and whether it matters to the business stay three separate things. Say what that changes for a reader reviewing the list.
slots.buyerIntent: How do I know who wrote each question?

slots.writingObjective: Caption the figure of this note in one or two factual sentences, grounded in the evidence it cites.

slots.heading: Demand decides what is measured, never the result
slots.writingObjective: Explain that demand data is used to choose what to measure and never to set the outcome; that the system refuses to attach a search volume to a single measured question; that demand strength can no longer be typed in by hand; and that it is derived from evidence or left absent.
slots.buyerIntent: Can a tool inflate how important a question looks?

slots.heading: Approving the list is one deliberate gesture
slots.writingObjective: Explain that approving the questions and starting the measurement are one atomic gate, and that the approval and the pre-registration of success criteria are the same gesture, so the yardstick cannot be chosen after the first results; that all objections to a draft list are returned at once; and that the system refuses to lock a list that could never show a change.
slots.buyerIntent: What happens when I press approve?

slots.heading: What gets measured is what you approved, nothing else
slots.writingObjective: Explain that the version measured is the version approved, and that any change to the list requires a new approval. Say why this matters when comparing before and after.
slots.buyerIntent: Can the list drift after I approve it?

slots.heading: What to ask any AI visibility vendor about its questions
slots.writingObjective: Give the buyer a short list of questions to put to any vendor, one per sentence, drawn from the mechanisms this note describes. Recommendations only, no claim about TextOS.

slots.heading: Where to go next
slots.writingObjective: Point the reader to the related notes. No claim about TextOS.
